slow_update_content:
Before choosing the strongest statement, establish which options are actually true under the stated hypotheses. Then compare only the valid options. Do not prefer a claim because it is more detailed, numerically larger, logically stronger, or resembles a familiar theorem. Never fill gaps with phrases such as “typically,” “likely,” or “the standard result” and then treat the guess as proof. For a specialized result, identify the exact theorem or derive the claim from the definitions; do not invent a critical threshold, extra hypothesis, lower bound, localization property, or supercritical regime by analogy. If the information provided does not justify an upgrade, do not make it.

Read every option literally: check its quantifiers, parameter range, endpoint, constant dependence, and whether it asserts necessity, sufficiency, an upper bound, a lower bound, or an equivalence. In particular, an O-bound does not give a matching lower bound; a fixed-time estimate is not uniform in time; and a more restrictive-looking option is not correct merely because it would be stronger if true.

Use these exact results when these patterns recur:
• For every knot type K and every p in (-1, infinity], rho_p(K) <= rho_p(U). Do not invent a failure threshold at p = 2.
• For n > 2, an irreducible root lattice of type X_n over O exists exactly when c(X_n) belongs to K, not when it belongs to O.
• Every order A in the stated three-sphere rational cohomology algebra has a CW realization with integral cohomology ring exactly A; do not weaken this to an isomorphism only after quotienting by torsion.
• In the stated adelic result, the projective image is K-rational; the upgrade to the adelic point being in X(K) uses point separation by A^m, not merely finiteness onto the image.
• For the sphere-packing densities, the uniform claim is delta_n >= delta_n^L >= c n^2 2^(-n). Do not assert a uniform relative gap between delta_n and delta_n^L without proof.
• In the regular-graph plus random-graph triangle-packing result, assert coverage of all but o(n^2) edges only; do not add localization of the uncovered edges.
• There exist monomorphisms F_n -> F_2 whose equalizer has rank at least 2n-2. A subgroup of a finitely generated free group can have rank greater than the ambient rank, so do not infer rank(Eq) <= n merely from Eq being a subgroup.
• For the stated genus-one band twist, S-equivalence holds exactly when a_22 = 0 and a_12 + a_21 divides ell, not 2ell.
• Under the fixed-size block-weighted law, the block tree is subcritical for u < u_C and critical for u >= u_C; do not infer a supercritical regime for u > u_C.
• For H(n,m), use n congruent to 0 modulo 6 and m congruent to 2 modulo n. With 0 <= m < n, this forces m = 2; do not replace the modulus by n/3 or n/2.
• For the stated dimension-19 kissing-number choices, use the established bound k(19) >= 11948; do not select the largest listed number unless it is verified as a valid bound.
• For the stated elliptic-equation existence result, use K_gamma = C_n gamma and alpha_gamma <= exp(-c_n K_gamma). Do not add a lower bound for alpha_gamma.

Preserve exact scope in other recurring estimates as well: the IBVP regularity is C((0,T)), not an assumed endpoint upgrade; the global homogenization estimate includes epsilon times [C + (n/2) log(max{t,epsilon}/epsilon)], not just a fixed-time bound; the hypercube variation supremum is unbounded for every finite r; and the random-graph cop-number conclusion is the high-probability O(sqrt(n) log n) upper bound unless a matching lower bound is established. Check formula conventions before committing: if a(p) counts anchors away from the origin, the anchored-weight denominator is a(p); derive the ruin exponent from the model, which here is u^(1-gamma); and apply congruence conditions using the full stated modulus and parameter range.
